Nearly 2,300 people were arrested across France when violence broke out around student-led protest marches yesterday.
About 1,000 police officers were also injured.
NPR's Eleanor Beersley reports the destruction could cost France upwards of hundreds of billions of dollars.
You get off the metro at Madeline and there's still the smoke burnt smell in the air.

President Trump continues his campaign rallies for GOP candidates this week.
Tomorrow he'll be in Kansas and with midterm elections nearing and Pierre's Mara Lison reports,
Democratic candidates are raising more money than their Republican opponents.
All through this election cycle, Republican campaign committees and billionaire super PACs have been swamping their Democratic equivalents.
Elon Musk, for instance, has spent more than $150 million in Texas to help the Republican Senate candidate there, Ken Paxton.
But according to the latest campaign finance filings, Paxton's Democratic opponent, James Talarico,
raised six times as much as Paxton himself this quarter.
Donations to individual candidates are usually a good proxy for voter enthusiasm.
And this year, the enthusiasm gap favors Democrats.
Democratic candidates in other key Senate races, including Alaska, Ohio, Maine, Michigan and Iowa,
have also outraised their Republican opponents.
Mara Lison, NPR News.
President Trump has announced plans to renovate the East Potomac Golf Links in Washington, D.C.
The goal, according to his Truth Social Post, is to turn it into a place that could host world class tournaments such as the PGA Championship or the U.S. Open.
NPR's Andrew Limbong reports.
At the East Potomac Golf Links, you can play nine or 18 holes at a fairly reasonable price or you can just hang out at the park area.
A D.C. preservation group had sued earlier to try and stop the administration from renovating the course,
arguing that tailoring it for the pros will inflate prices.
The National Park Service had already started cutting down trees in the area until last week when a district court judge ordered the government to stop.
The government then filed paperwork asking the judge to accuse herself from the case, accusing her of bias.
According to the Truth Social Post, renovations are due to start mid-November.
The next hearing for the golf course is scheduled for this week.
This is NPR.
An Air Force service member died last night after an accident during a pregame ceremony during a college football game in San Antonio.
Texas Public Radio's Jerry Clayton reports.
The incident occurred at the Alamo Dome ahead of the University of Texas-San Antonio's football game against Navy.
The airmen fell while repelling from the stadium's rafters during a salute to armed forces and veterans' pregame ceremony.
Nellis Air Force Base in Nevada confirmed the airmen died at a San Antonio hospital from injuries sustained in the fall.
The service member was assigned to Detachment 2 of the 6th Combat Training Squadron,
which operates out of joint-based San Antonio Camp Bullis and is part of a squadron headquartered at Nellis.
The game went ahead following the incident, which delayed the start of play.
The service member's identity has not been released.
I'm Jerry Clayton in San Antonio.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky says President Trump is still an ally.
But in an interview on NBC's Meet the Press, he warned that formally siding with Russia's leader would be an historic mistake.
It will not help us. And it will not help United States, I'm sure.
But, I mean, it's not my choice. And I hope that he will change his decisions, change his attitude to Putin.
During the interview, he suggested the U.S. government may have been responsible for an interruption to his country's use of the Starlink satellite,
which helps support military intelligence and save lives as Russia continues its strikes against Ukraine.
I'm Dua Lisa Kautau, NPR News in New York City.
